# World-model deck - outline and speaker notes (generated by build_deck.py)

## Slide 1: Title

- A hybrid physics + neural world model that predicts how human drivers react to CAV controllers, and how much each plan changes traffic delay, with uncertainty.

**Notes:** One sentence: the model is a hybrid. Physics (real controller code, IDM car-following, MOBIL lane change) plus a neural correction for how human drivers respond, and a head that outputs a distribution of the change in total delay for a candidate CAV plan. The talk is an honest status of that model.

## Slide 2: Why a world model: whether a controller helps depends on how human drivers react

- RSU chooses CAV controllers
- Benefit depends on human-driver reaction
- Need a model of the reaction: predicted delay change + uncertainty

**Notes:** Context only. An RSU at a highway merge can ask CAVs to drive in different ways (controllers). Whether a controller reduces total delay depends on how the surrounding human drivers react, and that reaction is not directly observable. So we need a model of that reaction that can score a candidate controller before it is used. The rest of the talk is about that model.

## Slide 3: Inputs: only what the RSU can see, turned into a state encoding

- Snapshot: up to 192 vehicles (position, speed, lane); entrance counters
- No hidden driver types or penetration
- Snapshot -> state encoder

**Notes:** The model input is a snapshot of up to 192 vehicles: for each, position, speed and lane, tagged as CAV self-reported or detected neighbour, plus entrance counters. Hidden driver types and true penetration are never inputs. A state encoder turns the snapshot into one representation used by both the dynamics and the effect head.

## Slide 4: Architecture: physics rollout for the dynamics, a plan-aware head for the delay change

- Snapshot -> encoder -> (a) dynamics (real controller code; IDM + MOBIL + neural correction; 0.5 s) and (b) effect head
- Effect head: 19 quantiles at 30/60/120/300/570 s = TRAIN average + gate x correction; 120 s plan summary
- Ranking loss within a decision; per-horizon loss scaling
- Arrival head and driver-response contrast: training signals

**Notes:** Snapshot goes through the encoder, then two parts. (a) Dynamics: CAVs are driven by the real controller code under the candidate plan; human drivers follow IDM car-following and MOBIL lane change plus a learned neural correction that gives an acceleration distribution and a lane-change decision; everything is rolled forward every 0.5 s. (b) Effect head: outputs the change in total delay versus native at 30, 60, 120, 300 and 570 s as 19 quantiles from 5% to 95%. It equals the TRAIN average effect plus a gate times a learned correction, so an untrained head reproduces the average. It is plan aware: it reads a 120 s summary of CAV motion (count, mean speed, min speed per 10 s bin). Training adds a ranking loss within a decision and per-horizon loss scaling. The arrival head and the driver-response contrast are training signals only.

## Slide 5: How it learns: replay the same traffic moment under different controllers

- Freeze one SUMO moment; replay under native / PI / other plans
- Label = delay(plan) - delay(native) from identical start
- Losses: one-step + multi-step driver acceleration, effect quantile loss, ranking loss

**Notes:** We freeze one SUMO traffic moment, so the start is identical, and replay it under different controllers. The difference in total delay between a plan and native, from the identical start, is the true effect label. Losses: one-step and multi-step driver acceleration loss for the neural correction, a quantile (pinball) loss on the effect, and a ranking loss within each decision.

## Slide 6: Is there something to predict? Controller effects are 5-27x larger than noise

- Chart: sd ratio per horizon with 90% CI (log scale)
- All lower CI bounds > 1 (16.3, 5.1, 4.0, 12.2, 3.0)
- Seed change = exactly 0

**Notes:** 90 runs, 30 TRAIN worlds x (R0 true native, N1 one-CAV nudge, S1 seed+1). R0 reproduces native bit-exactly. S1 is bit-identical to R0, so the seed floor is exactly zero. sd(PI-native)/sd(N1-native): 27.17 [16.32, 44.71] at 30 s, 9.42, 6.40, 20.82, 4.96 [3.00, 1724.41] at 570 s. Caveat: the nudge spread is itself heavy-tailed at 570 s. Source: WM-N1-NOISEFLOOR-20261004/RESULT.md.

## Slide 7: Prediction quality: calibrated and better than the average at long horizon, worse at 30 s

- Chart: CRPS ratio to TRAIN average per horizon, A8..A12 (+A13 pending)
- A11 / A12 at 30 s: 11.0 / 11.4 vs 5.3; at 300 s: 431.7 / 427.1 vs 528.2
- A13 = per-horizon gate + shift penalty + type-balanced training: PENDING

**Notes:** CRPS (lower better) on CAL-tune PI-native, 11 decisions, divided by the TRAIN-average (climatology) CRPS; below 1 beats the average. A11 CRPS: 11.0 / 37.3 / 135.3 / 431.7 / 1567.4 vs climatology 5.3 / 25.0 / 129.1 / 528.2 / 1563.6. A12: 11.4 / 40.8 / 135.8 / 427.1 / 1553.6 (REPORT.md of WM-N1-SCORE-A12-20261005). A8-A10 from MORNING_SUMMARY_20261005. A12 did not fix 30 s (11.4 vs 5.3, significantly worse); keeps the 300 s gain (427.1 vs 528.2, CI [-261, 38]). A13 = per-horizon gate + penalty on the actual shift away from the average + controller-type-balanced training; result expected 18:05.

## Slide 8: Does the prediction lead to better choices? Not yet: the replication did not confirm it

- Chart: regret at 300 s, evaluation slice vs fresh-world replication
- Slice: 972.3 vs 1555.8, CI [-1339, -3]
- Replication: 1072.7 vs 1117.2, diff CI [-224.8, 112.9] -> not replicated
- A9 / A10 / A12 also tie native

**Notes:** Decision test of the model's ranking ability: choose the plan with the best predicted delay and compare the regret with always-native (regret = s of total delay vs the best plan, lower is better). Evaluation slice (11 worlds, A11 chosen here): A11 972.3 vs always-native 1555.8 at 300 s, 90% CI of the difference [-1339, -3]. Pre-registered replication on 30 fresh worlds: A11 1072.7 vs native 1117.2, difference CI [-224.8, 112.9] includes 0, so NOT replicated; A9/A10/A12 also tie native. Message: the model does not yet separate situations well enough; the replication caught a selection effect (the model was picked on the slice).

## Slide 9: Diagnosis: the model's imagined future was a closed road

- Rollout animated only the snapshot cars: no exits or entries
- Same TRAIN situation, PI effect at 300 s: real-future summary +1355 s, closed-road +3732 s, true +1123 s
- Chart: CAVs on the road per 10 s bin: recorded vs closed road vs open road

**Notes:** The rollout animated only the cars in the snapshot: no vehicle left the road and none entered. CAVs therefore never exited, so the plan summaries (count, speed) fed to the effect head were unrealistic, which inflated the predictions. Same TRAIN situation (w8676m2700p20t360, PI at 300 s): summary from the real recorded future gives +1355 s, the closed-road rollout summary gives +3732 s, the true effect is +1123 s. Source: E:/rd-wt/rollout-entry/_out/ENTRY_FIX.md (the brief quoted +1356 for the real-future value; the report table says 1355, JSON 1354.67).

## Slide 10: Fix (tonight, exploratory, TRAIN): open-road rollout; magnitude fixed, ranking still weak

- 8 TRAIN states: MAE closed 3564 -> exits 961 -> open road 947 vs real plan 761; corr 0.45/0.35/0.37/0.52
- Smoke: 0 collisions; predictions +80..+540 s (was ~+3700), still picks native
- Remaining: rollout too fast/smooth (22-27 vs 16-23 m/s), no queues; weak ranking

**Notes:** Open-road rollout: vehicles exit at the road end and new vehicles enter using the observed entrance counters (rate = mean of the 12 most recent 10 s bins, Poisson per 0.5 s step). 8 TRAIN states, PI effect at 300 s, mean absolute error vs the true effect: closed road 3564 s, exits only 961, open road 947, real recorded plan 761; correlation with the true effect 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.37 / 0.52. Closed-loop smoke (TRAIN, 180 s): 360 rows, 0 collisions, 0 teleports. Predictions are now +80..+540 s instead of a flat +3700 s, and the planner still picks native. Remaining gap: rollout speeds too fast and smooth (mean 22-27 vs recorded 16-23 m/s), no queues, ranking weak. Exploratory: not a claim. Source: E:/rd-wt/rollout-entry/_out/ENTRY_FIX.md.

## Slide 11: Physics vs learning at short horizons: the closed-road rollout is nearly blind to the effect

- 60 TRAIN pairs
- Rollout sd 0.7 vs true 25 s at 30 s
- Rollout CRPS worse than average at 30/60/120 s; blend not significantly better

**Notes:** Blend check, TRAIN only, fixed 60 PI-vs-native pairs, no new simulation. The closed-road rollout's effect has mean near 0 and sd 0.67 / 3.06 / 8.04 s at 30 / 60 / 120 s versus true sd 24.95 / 104.6 / 327.3 s. Its CRPS is significantly worse than the TRAIN average at all three horizons (CI excludes 0). A rollout+head blend is not significantly better than the average at 30 and 60 s and worse at 120 s. Conclusion: need the open-road, queue-faithful rollout before giving physics weight at short horizons. Source: E:/rd-wt/blend-check/_out/BLEND_CHECK.md.
